title: Emergence From Local Rules
description: Weight three local steering rules and predict the flock-level pattern that no individual agent computes.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Leverage Points -- Rules, Paradigms, and Emergence
chapter_title: Leverage Points -- Rules, Paradigms, and Emergence

educational.learningObjective: Given a small set of local interaction rules, the learner will predict the emergent global pattern the agents will produce as a group, then compare that prediction against the running simulation.
learningOutcomes: Predict a global pattern from a set of local rule weights
Explain why changing a rule is a stronger intervention than changing a parameter
Distinguish information available to an agent from information available to an observer
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a set of three slider values and ask them to describe the resulting flock pattern in one sentence before running it.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Three-parameter agent simulation with observer-level pattern description
pedagogical.feedbackType: Continuous visual pattern formation plus a periodic plain-language description
misconceptionsAddressed: That some agent must know the group's plan
That the observer's description of the pattern is available to the agents
discussionQuestions: Meadows ranks rules above parameters as leverage points. Does this simulation support that?
What are the three local rules in a busy hallway or a checkout queue?
If you wanted to change the flock's shape, would you rather change a rule or add a leader?
